problem: Zero-shot LLM/VLM ObjectNav methods rely on scene-agnostic commonsense from web text rather than embodied 3D experience, and the episodic memories they build are discarded after each episode, so no lifelong experience accumulates.
motivation: Humans combine short-term memory with long-term memory that consolidates past experience to support decisions. Raw RGB-D trajectories are highly redundant (revisits, loops, overlapping runs), so a compact, retrievable representation is needed to store and reuse navigation experience.
key_idea: Store past navigation trajectories as compact topological-polar (topo-polar) graphs in a hierarchical coarse-to-fine RAG, and retrieve similar past trajectories for candidate frontier paths to guide an LLM planner's waypoint selection.
insight: Structured, order-preserving geometric-semantic encoding matters. Topo-polar sectors with both geometry and semantics reach 61.7 SR on HM3Dv1, versus 53.9 for textual neighbor aggregation and 57.3 for semantics only. Both retrieval stages are needed: removing coarse layout retrieval drops SR to 54.3, and replacing the trained sequence encoder with a text embedding gives 57.8. Experience also transfers across datasets, since a corpus from MP3D alone gives 59.8 on HM3Dv1, and combining corpora is best.
method: Topo-polar trajectory: skeletonize the free map, take junction pixels as nodes with non-maximum distance suppression (0.5 m), and describe each node by 12 polar sectors (30° each, 1.5 m radius) recording the first hit semantic, obstacle, unknown or free label. Assign poses to the nearest node, merge consecutive duplicates and prune loops.

Hierarchical chunking: each chunk holds a topo-polar trajectory, a language description and an embedding. Similar chunks are grouped into a merged topo-polar summary graph that serves as the coarse index.

Incremental construction: match new trajectories to summaries with rotation-invariant sector similarity, mutual KNN and RANSAC SE(2) alignment (inlier ratio). Merge into the group, discard trajectories with the same goal whose nodes are a subsequence of another's, or create a new group.
Fine index/trajectory encoder: a frozen DistilBERT node encoder, a DistilGPT2 sequence encoder and a goal embedding, trained with a contrastive loss (positives from the same group or same goal).

Navigation: build an open-vocabulary semantic map (GroundingDINO + MobileSAM), extract frontiers, run BFS over the topo-polar graph to get candidate paths, retrieve coarse-to-fine top-K experiences (text descriptions), and let Qwen3-32B pick the path at each new node. Execute with A*.
Corpus: built from HM3Dv1 and MP3D training splits (>200k and >150k sampled trajectories), frozen at test time.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-32B (frozen planner) + GroundingDINO + MobileSAM; DistilBERT (frozen) + DistilGPT2 trajectory encoder (contrastively trained)
setting.training_data: Trajectory encoder and RAG corpus built from HM3Dv1 train (>200k trajectories) and MP3D train (>150k trajectories); planner is training-free
setting.action_space: discrete actions, following an A* path to a frontier waypoint
setting.privileged: none at test time (the RAG is pre-built from training-split trajectories and frozen)

numbers.extra: RAG built from HM3Dv1+MP3D train trajectories

results: TrajRAG reaches SR/SPL of 42.6/18.0 on MP3D, 62.5/33.9 on HM3Dv1 and 78.1/40.2 on HM3Dv2. It beats the strongest baselines: ApexNAV on HM3Dv2 (76.2/38.0) and HM3Dv1 (59.6/33.0), BeliefMapNav on HM3Dv1 SR (61.4), and GOAL on MP3D SR (41.7). It also outperforms text-based RAG (53.3 SR) and GraphRAG (55.2 SR) variants.
limitations: The corpus is pre-built from training-split trajectories, and online test-time updating is supported but not evaluated.
The planner is a 32B LLM queried at every new topo-polar node, which is costly, and the paper gives no latency analysis. Gains in SPL are modest.
Retrieval depends on the accuracy of open-vocabulary detection and segmentation; only simulator results are reported, with no real-robot tests.
